title: More weekly sets for a low-volume muscle
statement: Within the ranges studied, more weekly sets per muscle are linked to more muscle growth. Moving a muscle from low volume (under about 10 weekly sets) toward a moderate range is supported; extra benefit above about 20 weekly sets is uncertain.
population: Mostly young adults; few studies in trained people.
what_the_app_does: When a muscle gets fewer than 10 hard sets a week and you want it bigger, we can suggest adding sets toward 10, never above 20, within your session time.

title: Lifting less on low-HRV days
statement: Lowering lifting volume on days of low HRV improves results.
what_the_app_does: Would let a low readiness reduce today's lifting. Until the evidence is there, readiness never changes your plan.

title: Heavier loads for maximal strength
statement: Lower rep ranges on main lifts improve maximal strength more than higher rep ranges.
what_the_app_does: When you ask to get stronger, we can suggest heavier loads (about 3 to 6 reps) on your main multi-joint lifts, with longer rests, and keep other exercises at moderate reps.

title: Limiting weekly running increases
statement: A gradual weekly distance progression reduces running injuries.
what_the_app_does: Would limit how fast your weekly running distance rises.

title: Protein for muscle gain
statement: Protein intake target for muscle gain.
what_the_app_does: If your goal is muscle gain and your protein target is under 1.6 g per kg of body weight a day, we can suggest raising it to 1.6 g/kg.
